claims.author: Sjors
claims.harm: Stopping the node on a mismatch risks introducing an effective checkpoint that prevents normal sync if the snapshot commitment is malicious
claims.quote: I think this risks introducing a new effective checkpoint. If the snapshot were malicious, normal users couldn't sync

claims.author: Sjors
claims.quote: Maybe limit the scope of this PR by only _checking_ the latest hash, but not (yet) deleting the other hashes.
claims.request: Limit the scope of the PR by checking the latest hash without deleting the older commitments yet

claims.author: Sjors
claims.quote: It would be good to provide some numbers in the PR description.
claims.request: Provide benchmark numbers in the PR description showing minimal performance impact

claims.author: Sjors
claims.question: How does flushing chainstate to disk before hashing interact with current IBD flush frequency?
claims.quote: I'm not up to speed on how often and when we flush the chainstate to disk during IBD nowadays. How does this interact with that?

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: Introduce an option to skip the new AssumeUTXO hash check (may be a hidden option)
claims.request: Add a configuration option to bypass or ignore the AssumeUTXO hash check

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: So not checking the non-latest hashes is fine, but it's useful to keep them for visibility.
claims.request: Keep non-latest AssumeUTXO commitments in source for visibility instead of dropping them

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.question: What is the performance impact when hitting an AssumeUTXO commitment block during validation?
claims.quote: What's the performance impact when hitting such a block?

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: Crashing an IBD node on snapshot mismatch penalizes nodes with fully verified valid data while failing to protect snapshot users from following an incorrect chain
claims.quote: Doesn't this make the result of a release including bad snaphot data worse for everyone -- Alice who does IBD has her node crash despite having good data that she fully verified, and Bob who uses the bad snapshot still potentially fails to an incorrect chain

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.quote: Having predictable snapshot points (every 14112 blocks [per bip452]) would allow every node to calculate the appropriate hash... Including the block's muhash in the assumeutxo set would also probably work here
claims.request: Consider predictable snapshot points (e.g. BIP 452) or including the block's muhash in the AssumeUTXO commitment to make verification easier and less disruptive
